summary: Short-lived API keys receiving inconsistent 429s due to sampling-window misalignment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (SkylineMaps) reports spiking 429 responses when using a pool of short-lived API keys created by an internal worker orchestrator. Keys are valid and requests succeed intermittently; 429s appear to correlate with key rotation and when many ephemeral keys are used in parallel.

Impact:
- SkylineMaps ingestion pipeline (map tile annotation) sees ~15-30% request rejection with 429s during nightly fanout.
- Occurs in prod-us-west; dedicated capacity.
- Customer is blocked from meeting nightly SLA for ingestion-dependent analytics.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated GPU pool (prod-us-west).
- SDK: upstream Go SDK v1.5.2 calling REST endpoints via their proxy.
- Keys: ephemeral short-lived service keys (TTL ~2 minutes) minted by their orchestrator.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Mint N ephemeral keys in parallel: for i in 1..250 spawn key (TTL 120s)
2) For each key open a short-lived connection and issue 6 concurrent generation requests (seq length 128)
3) Observe returned status codes and X-RateLimit-* headers

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 429s across many keys within a ~60s window after rotation.
- X-RateLimit-Remaining headers sometimes show positive tokens while request still returns 429.
- Console shows no quota exhaustion at org level; token accounting appears fragmented among many ephemeral key IDs.

Expected behavior:
- Either consistent remaining tokens reported or smooth degradation (retry-after) when quota is actually exhausted.
- Short-lived keys should be aggregated against tenant/dedicated-pool accounting without double-counting at ingress.

Attached logs/headers (customer redacted):
- Request IDs: r-0a1b2c3d4e5f, r-9f8e7d6c5b4a
- Sample response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 350, Retry-After: 5, Status: 429
- Edge logs excerpt shows rapid token check calls originating from different NATed IPs (their proxy pool).

Notes from customer:
- This did not occur with a single long-lived key (reusing same key) — failure is amplified when using many ephemeral keys.
- They suspect a timing/sampling-window mismatch between edge proxy and origin rate-limiter where short TTLs cause re-registering of buckets and transient undercounting/overcounting.

Request from customer:
- Explain why ephemeral keys cause inconsistent 429s and recommend config/workarounds.
- If required, request a temporary priority lane or a dedicated burst pool for their nightly backfill while we investigate.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13: Initial triage by Support (Maya) — reproduced locally with smaller scale script; observed soft-429s after rotating keys rapidly.
2026-03-13: Pulled edge and origin telemetry for tenant; saw refill deltas misaligned between edge token caches and origin accounting during high key churn.

Hypothesis: Edge-level token caches use a different refill epoch/sampling window than origin rate-limiter; when keys are short-lived and recreated, edge may treat them as new buckets and preflight checks can cause transient double-deductions or racey refills.

Checked recent deploys: no rate-limiter release in last 48hrs. However, nginx sidecar update deployed to a subset of edge nodes on 2026-03-12 — possible header normalization/connection reuse change (see linked PR).
Parallel issue references: SUP-76121 (early 429s during mass concurrent upload), SUP-3141596 (uneven 429s long-lived vs short-lived keys).
comments: 2026-03-13 09:42 - Support (Maya): Hi SkylineMaps team — thanks for the detailed repro. We're triaging now. Can you confirm whether your orchestrator re-uses keys across requests or creates a new key per worker invocation? Also, please provide a few sample request-ids around a 429 event.

2026-03-13 10:12 - Customer (SkylineMaps - Jordan): We create a new key per worker run (so high churn). Sample IDs: r-0a1b2c3d4e5f, r-9f8e7d6c5b4a. We can throttle down the churn but need guidance for long-term solution.

2026-03-13 14:30 - SRE (Ravi): Reproduced with our load generator. Observed edge-cache hit then origin rejects; bucket TTL re-registration happens in <2s creating a small race window. Suspect epoch alignment between ingress and master rate-limiter. Opening instrumentation PR to add debug counters. (see https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2423)

2026-03-14 08:05 - Support (Maya): Temporary mitigation: recommend reusing keys for batches (reuse per worker for the lifespan of the job) and enable their SDK client-side backoff with jitter. We can also provision an isolated burst pool for nightly jobs — please confirm if SkylineMaps wants us to enable that while we deploy a fix.
workarounds: 1) Reuse an ephemeral key across a worker's batch instead of creating a new key per request.
2) Reduce the concurrency per-key (target 4 concurrent requests per key rather than 6) to reduce churn impact.
3) Enable client-side exponential backoff with jitter and honor Retry-After headers; set max retries to 3 for ingestion flows.
4) Request temporary isolated burst pool from Support (we can enable a short-term dedicated burst lane for nightly backfills).
next_steps: SRE to add debug counters to edge and origin to measure per-key register/unregister events and sampling window alignment (assigned to Ravi).
If counters confirm misalignment, plan a small config change to align edge refill epoch with origin (rollout to subset of edges).
Support to offer SkylineMaps temporary burst pool and track acceptance; if accepted, schedule a change with infra team and update the customer with ETA.
Follow-up run with customer after enabling mitigations (reduced churn + backoff) to confirm 429s drop below 1%.
